steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat in a large skillet. Add onion; cook and stir onions until softened about 5 minutes. Stir in bacon pieces and brown sugar, and cook until bacon pieces are crisp. Remove from skillet.
Spread 1/4 cup barbecue sauce on one tortilla. Sprinkle with 1/4 of the bacon and onion mixture, 1 tablespoon cilantro, and 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese. Top with a tortilla.

Heat 1 teaspoon olive oil over medium heat in a large skillet. Place the uncooked quesadilla in the skillet. Cook on one side until browned and crisp, about 3 minutes. Flip, and cook on the other side until the cheese is completely melted, about 2 minutes more. Remove to a paper towel lined plate to cool. Repeat with remaining six tortillas. Slice into quarters using a sharp knife or kitchen scissors when cool enough to handle.

raw_recipe.headline: Barbeque Bacon Quesadillas
raw_recipe.description: Barbeque sauce and bacon add an American twist to this simple, classic Mexican dish!

review.reviewBody: These are very good, the only change I would make is to cook onions and take out of skillet until the bacon is cooked, then add the onions and the brown sugar. If you do it as the recipe says, your onions will start to burn before you bacon is done.

This was just as delicious as it sounds. I loved every bite. I scaled this back to only make one serving, and I'm so glad I tried this. I used bacon that was leftover from breakfast, and it was already crispy, so I only cooked it with the onion until it was warmed through. The brown sugar dissolved into the dish quickly, but I forgot to scale it back, but I like sweet anyway, so it worked for me. I used Head Country BBQ sauce, which is a mix of smoky and spicy. Don't use a paper towel to let these cool, as the paper toweling stuck to the quesadilla where the bbq sauce filling started to bubble out. It was a pain to try to remove once it was stuck. I used dried cilantro as for some reason it doesn't have the detergent flavor that fresh has, but I also scaled back on it as it's not a favored herb. I minced the onion very finely as I dislike onion texture, and cooked them well over a lower heat so they wouldn't burn until they started to turn golden, then when I added the bacon and brown sugar, the onions practically disappeared. I am definitely making this again. I would precook the bacon as there is no way the bacon is going to get crisp before those onions burn. I took off a star just because that's a crucial step and while I used my own judgement and knowledge to modify it, a brand new cook might not know that. The addition of a little smoked chicken or pulled pork would make this even better. I made a meal off of this, and enjoyed every bite.

This was super yummy! I had some left over BBQ pulled pork to use up and wasn't in the mood for just pulled pork sandwiches. Someone from AR recommended this to me and I'm so glad they did! I used the BBQ pork in place of just the BBQ sauce. I also added some black beans and served with roasted salsa on the side. It's so nice to have something fun and different to do with leftovers! Will be making these again!

MMMMmmm this was good! super duper rich tho! Use less bbq sauce, just a thin layer is all you need. Use brown sugar bbq sauce vs adding brown sugar. After onions are soft remove from pan until bacon is almost cooked. Don't skip the cilantro this adds a nice balance of flavor!

Used homemade bbq sauce (Ball Blue Book) and vidalia onions. Served with French Onion sour cream on top and sweet slaw on the side. Only change I'll make next time is use a couple more slices of bacon, but I will definitely be making this many times in the future, wonderful taste and easy to make!

This was very tasty. I cooked the bacon first, chopped it, then added it to the cooking onions. I made the recipe quantity for the "stuffing" but served only to two people. A thin layer of barbecue sauce was needed. Another go-to quick meal!

I made these with shredded ham to use up the leftovers and they were fantastic! The only other change I made was to use less bbq sauce on each tortilla. I'll be using this recipe every time I have leftover ham. The whole family loved them!
The flavor was good but it was too greasy.
Great recipe! Cooked as per the directions but just used the BBQ sauce to taste. Going to try these again with some different fillings but the cilantro and BBQ is an awesome combo.
Made these as appetizers at our "non traditional" Thanksgiving dinner and they were a big hit with everyone!
this is a very good recipe but i say use less bbq sauce
These were a hit! I will definitely make them again. We were fighting over the last pieces!

I made this last night for a halloween party. It was the first thing to go. Everyone loved it. I left out the cilantro because 1) I don't like it and 2) I didn't have it on hand. But it was a huge hit. Will definitely make it again.
